status_reason: The target variable and the contaminant are undefined, so an exact sensor configuration cannot be chosen yet; the alternative depends on facts still missing.
answer: An exact sensor configuration should not be chosen before the contaminant or the quality variable is known, because for samples of unknown composition it is not possible to predict which method will work. The first step is a laboratory screen of on-specification and off-specification samples, with NIR as the first candidate for a liquid and Raman as the comparison method. The in-line configuration follows only after the screen shows which method sees the difference.

inline.headline: Test NIR transmission or transflection probe in a laboratory screen of on-specification and off-specification samples before any in-line configuration
inline.install: Laboratory first; in-line location to be decided after the screen
inline.not_final_because: The contaminant and the quality variable are unknown and no spectra or reference data exist yet; NIR is a first candidate for a liquid, not a proven method for this process.

problems.text: An exact configuration is requested before the analytical problem is known; selecting a method needs the analytical problem defined, and an immediate exact configuration would rest on invented facts.
Choosing a single best method blind is not supported for samples of unknown composition; several optical methods must be tested first to find the most suitable one or a combination.
Raman signals are weak and, for many organic compounds, can be masked by much stronger fluorescence, so Raman suitability for this liquid is unknown until tested.
Fluorescence would detect the contaminant only if it fluoresces, and most chemicals do not fluoresce.

methods.why: NIR is the most common online fiber-probe method for liquids and works with remote fiber probes, but its broad overlapping bands need chemometrics.
Raman needs special probes and carries information complementary to MIR and NIR, but its signal can be masked by fluorescence.
MIR ATR analyses liquids at a distance from the spectrometer and gives well-defined peaks, but MIR is limited to very thin layers and requires a mid-IR fiber.
Fluorescence is highly sensitive, but it depends on secondary emission that most chemicals lack.

questions.q: What is the suspected contaminant, and which quality variable goes off specification?
questions.why: The method and its target depend on the analytical problem, which is currently undefined.

questions.q: Is the liquid transparent, turbid, coloured, or high in fat or solids?
questions.why: Probe choice follows optical density: transmission for transparent liquids, ATR for opaque or concentrated media.

questions.q: Where in the process would the probe sit, and what is the pipe or vessel geometry and path length?
questions.why: Fiber and probe design follow the interface and the process location.

questions.q: Are off-specification samples available, with independent laboratory analyses of the suspected contaminant and quality variable?
questions.why: Spectra can only be linked to the off-specification event if reference analyses exist for the same samples.

questions.q: What are the specification limits, and how often do off-specification events occur?
questions.why: The go/no-go criteria and the sampling plan depend on these values.

experiment.objective: Find which optical method sees the difference between on-specification and off-specification liquid, before any in-line configuration.
steps: Collect on-specification and off-specification samples of the process liquid, with independent laboratory analyses of the suspected contaminant and quality variable.
Measure all samples in the laboratory with NIR transmission/transflection, a Raman probe and, if needed, MIR ATR.
Confirm that the fiber covers the measured range: Vis-NIR silica for NIR and Raman, and a mid-IR fiber for MIR ATR.
Identify the key spectral features that separate the classes and check whether a single method or a fused NIR + Raman model separates them better on the same validation data.
Only if a combination wins, plan the in-line configuration; if no method separates the classes, return to the sample definition.
references: S01 p.14 (Bogomolov et al., Sensors 17(11): 2548, cited in the S01 multispectral passage)
experiment.go_no_go: Criteria come from the client: the specification limit for the quality variable and the accepted error of the method.

pathway.key_features: Not yet known; they must be identified from laboratory spectra of on-specification and off-specification samples.
pathway.path_reason: The analytical problem is undefined, and the AFS pathway starts with multi-method laboratory trials before key features and a model can be chosen.

multispectral.why: NIR sees hydrogen bonds and polar groups while Raman sees the molecular backbone and non-polar groups, so their information is complementary; NIR + Raman gave the best results in the pellet coating process.
multispectral.test: Compare the fused NIR + Raman model with the best single-method model on the same independent validation set of on-specification and off-specification samples; keep the combination only if it wins.

assumptions: The process liquid can be sampled for laboratory tests.
The off-specification events are linked to a contaminant that is not yet identified.
The liquid may be transparent enough for a transmission probe, which is to be checked in the first screen.
